description: Extend the CI validation scope so `make ci` (6_deploy/scripts/ci_checks.sh) also validates the new 6_deploy/infra/codepipeline stack offline, making the Validate pipeline stage authoritative over the stack that manages the pipeline. Depends on FEAT-001 (the stack must exist and pass fmt/validate for the extended ci_checks.sh to go green). Small, single-file change.
steps:
Read 6_deploy/scripts/ci_checks.sh. After the existing agentcore-backends validation block (the one ending with `terraform test`), add a THIRD block mirroring the EKS-stack block (offline, no credentials, NO terraform test since this stack has no test suite):
```bash
echo "Validating Terraform files (CodePipeline stack)"
(
    cd 6_deploy/infra/codepipeline
    terraform fmt -check -recursive
    terraform init -backend=false >/dev/null
    terraform validate >/dev/null
)
```
Place it before the final `echo "CI checks passed"`.
Do not change any other validation block. Do not add a terraform test for this stack.
After verifying, set this FEAT's status to completed, record findings if useful, and git add 6_deploy/scripts/ci_checks.sh and commit locally on the worktree branch (do not push).
acceptance_criteria: `export PATH="$HOME/.spbc-deploy/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"; make ci` from the repo root runs green end to end, including a 'Validating Terraform files (CodePipeline stack)' step that fmt/init(-backend=false)/validates 6_deploy/infra/codepipeline.
ci_checks.sh still validates the EKS stack and the agentcore-backends stack (with terraform test) exactly as before — only an additional block was appended.
verification: export PATH="$HOME/.spbc-deploy/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"; cd /Users/cloudageglobal/Desktop/Ai_ML_GenAI_GenBI_AgenticAi_MultiAgentAi_HarnessEngineering/AgenticAI/Harness_project/.worktrees/codecommit-ci && make ci   # expect 'CI checks passed' and the new CodePipeline-stack validation line
findings:
Implemented as a single-block append to 6_deploy/scripts/ci_checks.sh. Added a third Terraform validation block immediately after the agentcore-backends block (the one ending in `terraform test`) and before the final `echo "CI checks passed"`:
```bash
echo "Validating Terraform files (CodePipeline stack)"
(
    cd 6_deploy/infra/codepipeline
    terraform fmt -check -recursive
    terraform init -backend=false >/dev/null
    terraform validate >/dev/null
)
```
No terraform test added for this stack (it has no test suite). The EKS and agentcore-backends blocks were left unchanged. No other files touched.

Verification command run (from worktree root, Terraform 1.16.6 on PATH via the .spbc-deploy export; AWS_REGION=eu-central-1, AWS_PAGER=""):
`export PATH="$HOME/.spbc-deploy/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"; make ci`
Result: exit 0. Output (in order): 'Running CI validations' -> 'Validating Terraform files (EKS stack)' -> 'Validating and testing Terraform files (AgentCore backends; mocked providers)' -> 'Validating Terraform files (CodePipeline stack)' -> 'CI checks passed'. The new CodePipeline-stack validation line appears and the run is green end to end.

All validation was static/offline (-backend=false, no AWS calls, no terraform apply, no create-repository). terraform init created .terraform/ and .terraform.lock.hcl locally; `git status` confirmed these are gitignored and NOT staged. Only 6_deploy/scripts/ci_checks.sh was committed.
